text.p: Following are analysts' views on telecommunications group Nokia's first-half earnings report, which included 94 percent growth in digital mobile phone sales and pretax profit above forecasts at 3.33 billion markka.
The mean forecast was for a 3.09 billion markka profit and the highest forecast was 3.30 billion.
"Those were very good results ... but after Ericsson, this was no knock-out surprise."
He said it was understandable if some investors wanted to take profits after the report since the good news was already priced in.
"I think the key thing there was that they had not been losing any significant market share in digital handsets, that was very comforting."
Nokia said growth in infrastructure was above market growth:
"At this share price, Nokia does not look overvalued." Nokia traded around 477.00 markka in Helsinki and around $86 in New York.
"After Nokia's and Ericsson's growing market shares and good results, it looks like someone else is losing."

"Given the company's strong track record there are a lot of reasons to wait and see if they will deliver a new top-end handset by the fourth quarter of 1997 (to rival Ericsson's high-end 788 and Motorola's StarTac)."
"Investors right now are looking for a new reason to buy Nokia and there's not really one in there (the report). That said, there's certainly no reason to sell because of the trend in these results."
